result:
Done. `bunx guren gate` passes every stage (codegen, typecheck, lint, check, audit, test), and the new feature test file has seven passing cases covering the worked example, refused edits, the revisions page props, restore, authorization for other users and guests, the wrong-post 404, and delete cleanup.

**What changed**

- `db/schema.ts` and `db/migrations/20260925052147_post_revisions/`: new `post_revisions` table with `id`, `post_id`, `title`, `excerpt`, `body`, `created_at` (ISO 8601 text, same default as `posts`).
- `app/Models/PostRevision.ts`: model with nothing fillable and a `keepFrom(post, { trx })` helper that copies the post's current title, excerpt and body. `Post` gained a `revisions` hasMany relation.
- `app/Http/Controllers/PostController.ts`: `update` keeps the pre-save version and applies the edit inside one transaction, so a refused save (422 or 403) keeps nothing. `destroy` deletes the post's revisions in the same transaction as the post.
- `app/Http/Controllers/PostRevisionController.ts`: `index` lists revisions newest first, `restore` copies the revision back onto the post after keeping the current version. Both authorize with the existing `update` policy ability, so non-authors get 403 and guests are redirected to `/login` by the `auth` middleware. A revision id belonging to another post throws a 404.
- `routes/web.ts`: `GET /posts/:id/revisions` (`posts.revisions.index`) and `POST /posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore` (`posts.revisions.restore`) inside the authenticated group.
- `app/Http/Resources/PostRevisionResource.ts` and `resources/js/pages/posts/Revisions.tsx`: the page receives `post` and `revisions: [{ id, postId, title, excerpt, body, createdAt }]` and offers a Restore button per row. `posts/Show.tsx` links the author to it next to Edit.
- `app/Http/Validators/PostValidator.ts`: `PostRevisionParamsSchema` for the `revisionId` param.
- `tests/PostRevisionController.test.ts`: the feature tests described above. Generated `.guren/*.gen.ts` manifests were regenerated.

Summary: I added post revisions to the blog app. A new `post_revisions` table and `PostRevision` model store the title, excerpt and body a post had before each successful edit or restore, written transactionally from `PostController.update` and the new `PostRevisionController.restore`; `PostController.destroy` removes a post's revisions with it. Two authenticated routes expose the author-only history page at `/posts/:id/revisions` (Inertia page `posts/Revisions` with `revisions` props newest first) and the restore action at `/posts/:id/revisions/:revisionId/restore`, which redirects to the post and answers 404 for a revision from another post. A migration, resource, page, a link from the post page, regenerated manifests, and a feature test suite round it out; `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` and the full `guren gate` all pass.
